correctness.rationale: With s=r², uniqueness for the scalar radial ODE makes every periodic trajectory constant in s; positive angular speed makes every positive root of Q into a circle with physical period 2π/Ω(s_i). In angular time, differentiate ds/dθ=2sQ(s)/Ω(s) at the root and evolve for angle 2π. This gives log μ_i=2s_iT_iQ′(s_i), so hyperbolicity is simple-root multiplicity and the exact absence of extra circles forces Q/A to have one constant nonzero sign on (0,∞). For the converse, squared Lagrange cardinal functions interpolate both the positive signed radial quotient values and the positive angular speeds; their common zero set is empty since the original cardinal functions sum to 1. This proves strict positivity, node values and the upper degrees max(deg Q, deg Ω)≤3N−2. For any fixed radii and periods, choose signed quotient values (1,ε,…,ε). If there were qualifying degree ≤2N−3 positive quotients for arbitrarily small ε, bounded coefficient sequences would have a nonnegative limit with N−1 double interior zeros and value 1 at the first node. Unbounded sequences have a nonzero limit after coefficient normalization, with N double interior zeros, since all original node values remain bounded. Both cases contradict the degree cap. There is no cancellation of radial and angular leading terms (restrict to y=0, where they are separate Cartesian components), so degree is precisely 2 max(deg Q,deg Ω)+1. N=1 requires a nonconstant Q and permits degree 3 for every admissible datum. The two-circle witness independently gives the root 13/3 of the unique affine radial quotient and multiplier exponents −12π and 24π/5. The all-N proof is analytic; the frozen rational checker was inspected, not executed. No claim holds here about unrestricted planar fields or forward completeness.
